title: Detector 'marginal' path skips the PSD floor and reinterprets eps_floor: user-supplied psd with a zero bin yields nan where 'matched' is finite
evidence: nufft_lrt.py:39-42 `_whitened_inner` divides by `psd` directly; :483-485 for `estimate_psd=False` run() only does `psd = np.asarray(psd, dtype=self.real_type)` (no floor); the matched path floors inside `_compute_matched_filter_snr` :600 `P_s = np.maximum(P_s, eps_floor * np.median(P_s[P_s > 0]))`, but `_marginal_statistic` never floors and uses `eps_floor` as an ABSOLUTE cutoff on the whitened template norm :88 `if den <= eps_floor: return 0.0`. Reproduced on CPU with the conftest stubs (scratchpad/check_eps_floor.py): psd=ones with psd[3]=0 -> `_compute_matched_filter_snr` = 47710.5, `_marginal_statistic` K=0 = nan, K=1 = nan; a 1e-7-scaled template with eps_floor=1e-6 -> marginal 0.0 vs matched -0.9992. The same kwarg therefore means two different things depending on `detector`, and only one detector is protected against a degenerate psd.
recommendation: Apply the median-relative PSD floor once in run() for every detector (right after psd is set, before `_statistic` is built), remove the floor from `_compute_matched_filter_snr` or make it a no-op, and give `_marginal_statistic` a separate, documented denominator guard (or reuse the K=0 `den > 0` check). Add a CPU test in TestDetectorAlgebra that a zero psd bin gives identical, finite behaviour for 'matched' and 'marginal'.

title: sparse_bls_cpu (and by code inspection the GPU BLS paths) silently return a finite, plausible periodogram for NaN times/fluxes and for dy=0; no public entry point validates finiteness
evidence: scratchpad/validation_probe.py (conftest stubs, CPU): `sparse_bls_cpu NaN in y  OK tuple [(40,), 40] dtype0=float32 has_nan=False`; `sparse_bls_cpu NaN in t  OK ... has_nan=False`; `sparse_bls_cpu dy=0 (inf weight)  OK ... has_nan=False  warnings: divide by zero encountered in power`; `sparse_bls_cpu NaN freq  OK`; `sparse_bls_cpu freq<=0  OK`; `single_bls dy=0  OK int 0`; `single_bls q>1 OK int 0`, `single_bls q<0 OK int 0`; `utils.autofrequency NaN t  OK ndarray ... has_nan=True`. No `isfinite` check exists in bls.py's preprocessing (bls.py:1516-1524, 1863-1873, 2077-2086 only cast/epoch-subtract) nor in tls.py:649-651 / tls.py:1113 _preprocess_batch. test_error_hygiene.py only promises typed exceptions and no asserts; RELEASE_NOTES 'Typed exceptions ... clear messages' implies validation that does not exist for NaN/inf. docs/source/bls.rst:285-287 says near-zero dy is the user's job, but dy == 0 (inf weight -> NaN weights) is not a 'floor' question, it is garbage-in.
recommendation: Add one shared host-side validator (e.g. utils._check_lightcurve(t, y, dy): non-empty, equal lengths, all finite, dy > 0; and _check_freqs(freqs): finite, > 0) and call it at the top of every public entry point (eebls_gpu*, sparse_bls_*, single_bls, eebls_transit*, tls_search_*, tls_search_batch, and normalize_light_curves used by LS/CE/PDM run). title: GPUAsyncProcess accepts device=, reader=, function_kwargs= and silently ignores all three (device selection is actually CUDA_DEVICE env var)
evidence: base/async_process.py:13-16: `self.reader = kwargs.get('reader', None)` / `self.function_kwargs = kwargs.get('function_kwargs', {})` / `self.device = kwargs.get('device', 0)`. `grep -rn "self\.device\|'device'" cuvarbase/*.py cuvarbase/base/*.py` returns only that assignment; `grep -rn "self\.reader\|function_kwargs"` likewise returns only base/async_process.py:13,15. context.py:7-9 and README 'Installation' notes: device selection 'follows the CUDA_DEVICE environment variable'. Every process class (LombScargleAsyncProcess, ConditionalEntropyAsyncProcess, PDMAsyncProcess, NFFTAsyncProcess, NUFFTLRTAsyncProcess) inherits this, so `LombScargleAsyncProcess(device=1)` runs on device 0 with no error.
recommendation: Delete the three dead kwargs from GPUAsyncProcess.__init__ (nothing reads them) and, for `device`, raise ValueError('use the CUDA_DEVICE environment variable before first GPU use') so 1.0 does not freeze a no-op parameter. Add a class docstring to GPUAsyncProcess (it is in __all__ and has none) listing the kwargs that are honored (nstreams).

title: tls_search_gpu keeps a public `durations=` parameter that 'has never been used by any TLS path' (warns and ignores); n_durations is likewise a warned no-op outside Keplerian mode
evidence: tls.py:422-423 signature `def tls_search_gpu(t, y, dy, periods=None, durations=None, ...)`; docstring tls.py:452-456 `durations : array_like, optional / Unused; accepted for backward compatibility only (a warning is raised if passed)`; tls.py:547-552 `warnings.warn("tls_search_gpu: the `durations` parameter has never been used by any TLS path and is ignored; ...")` (plain UserWarning, not DeprecationWarning). tls.py:598-603 `warnings.warn("n_durations is only honored in Keplerian mode (qmin/qmax provided); the standard TLS duration grid is fixed at 15 log-spaced durations")`. TLS has never been published (PyPI latest is 0.2.5), so there is nothing to be backward compatible with.
recommendation: Remove `durations` from the tls_search_gpu signature before 1.0 (callers get a natural TypeError). Either honor `n_durations` on the non-Keplerian fast path (tls_search_batch already takes n_durations and fixed qmin/qmax arrays at tls.py:594-597, so passing n_durations through is a one-line change) or raise ValueError instead of warning. Re-run the TLS GPU tests.

evidence: bls.py:1392 signature `dlogq=0.2` vs bls.py:1436 `dlogq: float, optional, (default: 0.5)` (line 1437 also has flake8 W605 `d\log q` in the same docstring). bls.py:953 `max_nblocks: int, optional (default: 200)` vs eebls_gpu_fast signature `max_nblocks=5000`. ce.py:176 `mag_bins: int, optional (default: 10)` vs ce.py:214 `self.mag_bins = kwargs.get('mag_bins', 5)`. cunfft.py:177 `sigma: float, optional (default: 2)` vs cunfft.py:212 `kwargs.get('sigma', 4)`; cunfft.py:183 `autoset_m: bool, optional (default: True)` vs cunfft.py:214 `kwargs.get('autoset_m', False)`. tls.py:526-534 Returns lists keys `'best_t0'`, `'best_duration'`, `'best_depth'`, `'SDE' (if computed)` but the function returns `'best_t0_per_period'`, `'best_duration_per_period'`, `'best_depth_per_period'`, `'period'`, `'T0'`, `'duration'`, `'depth'`, `'SDE'`, `'SDE_raw'`, `'SNR'`, `'FAP'`, `'power'`, `'SR'`, ... (tls.py:624-647); tls.py:537-538 `For the first implementation, it provides a basic version that will be optimi
recommendation: Fix each docstring to the actual default/key set (or change the code default where the docstring is the intent — e.g. NFFT autoset_m: the CHANGELOG advertises autoset_m as the rigorous default, decide which). Replace the tls_search_gpu Returns block with the real key list and drop the 'Phase 2' note. Fix the LombScargleAsyncProcess example to `results = proc.run([...]); freqs, powers = results[0]`. title: New-in-1.0 entry points expose 14-30 positional parameters (tls_search_gpu, tls_search_batch, eebls_gpu_batch, keplerian_freq_grid) — the exact hazard the sparse_bls keyword-only change fixed
evidence: AST dump: `tls_search_gpu(t, y, dy, periods=None, durations=None, qmin=None, qmax=None, n_durations=15, R_star=1.0, M_star=1.0, period_min=None, ... , nbins=None, **kwargs)` = 30 positional-or-keyword params; `tls_search_batch(lightcurves, R_star=1.0, M_star=1.0, R_planet=1.0, periods=None, qmin=None, ...)` = 22; `eebls_gpu_batch(lightcurves, freqs, qmin=0.01, qmax=0.5, noverlap=2, dlogq=0.3, dphi=0.0, ...)` = 14; `keplerian_freq_grid(period_min, period_max, baseline, R_star=1.0, M_star=1.0, oversampling=2, return_qvals=False)`. Contrast `sparse_bls_cpu(t, y, dy, freqs, *, qmin=None, ...)` and CHANGELOG.rst:34: `**BREAKING:** all sparse_bls_cpu/sparse_bls_gpu arguments after freqs are keyword-only — pre-1.0 positional calls ... would have silently landed on the new qmin parameter and returned an all-zero periodogram`. Inserting a parameter into any of the 1.0-new signatures later would be a silent breaking change for positional callers for the whole 1.x line.
recommendation: Insert a bare `*` after the data/grid arguments in the functions that have no released user base: tls_search_gpu (after `periods`), tls_search_batch (after `lightcurves`), tls_transit (after `dy`), eebls_gpu_batch (after `freqs`), keplerian_freq_grid/uniform_freq_grid (after `baseline`), convert_bls_power (after `dy`). Leave the pre-1.0 BLS signatures (eebls_gpu, eebls_gpu_fast*, eebls_transit*) alone. Grep tests/scripts for positional use of those params first.

title: TLS entry points hard-reject R_star > 3.5 or M_star > 2.0 via validate_stellar_parameters with no override on tls_search_gpu/tls_search_batch/tls_transit
evidence: tls_grids.py:437-466 `def validate_stellar_parameters(R_star=1.0, M_star=1.0, R_star_min=0.13, R_star_max=3.5, M_star_min=0.1, M_star_max=2.0)` raises `ValueError(f"R_star={R_star} outside allowed range ...")`. tls.py:541 and tls.py:1256 call `tls_grids.validate_stellar_parameters(R_star, M_star)` with no way to pass the bounds; the bound kwargs are not in the tls_search_gpu/tls_search_batch/tls_transit signatures (AST dump). Probe: `validate_stellar_parameters R=5  RAISE ValueError: R_star=5.0 outside allowed range [0.13, 3.5] solar radii`, `M=3  RAISE ValueError ... [0.1, 2.0]`. A subgiant/A-star host cannot be searched at all.
recommendation: Plumb `R_star_min/R_star_max/M_star_min/M_star_max` through tls_search_gpu, tls_search_batch and tls_transit (the reference transitleastsquares exposes the same overrides), or downgrade the check to a warning. Document the default bounds in tls.rst 'Input conventions'.

title: Same public name, different first argument: bls.q_transit(freq, rho) vs tls_grids.q_transit(period, R_star, M_star, R_planet) (plus a third private copy bls_frequencies._q_transit)
evidence: bls.py:277 `def q_transit(freq, rho=1., **kwargs)`; tls_grids.py:24 `def q_transit(period, R_star=1.0, M_star=1.0, R_planet=1.0)`; bls_frequencies.py:18 `def _q_transit(freq, rho=1.0)`. Probe: `bls.q_transit(0.5) vs tls_grids.q_transit(0.5): 0.0478 vs 0.1212` (same call, 2.5x different answer). docs/source/bls.rst:165 instructs `from cuvarbase.bls import sparse_bls_cpu, q_transit` while docs/source/tls.rst documents the tls_grids one; neither docstring warns about the other.
recommendation: Do not rename bls.q_transit (pre-1.0 API). Add a first-line note to both docstrings ('takes FREQUENCY [c/d]; see tls_grids.q_transit for the period/stellar-parameter form' and vice versa), and make bls_frequencies._q_transit call bls.q_transit (or vice versa) so there is one implementation of the Keplerian duty-cycle relation. title: Frequency-grid argument handling differs per process: CE rejects a float32 freqs array (README teaches float32) with a misleading 'number of frequency grids' error; LS/PDM accept it
evidence: ce.py:508 and ce.py:590 `elif isinstance(frqs[0], float): frqs = [frqs] * len(data)` — `np.float32` is not a subclass of Python float, so a float32 array falls through to ce.py:511-514 `raise ValueError("number of frequency grids (%d) does not match number of lightcurves (%d)")` with len(freqs) as the 'grid count'. pdm.py:241,353 use `isinstance(frqs[0], (float, np.floating))`; lombscargle.py:834 uses `elif not isinstance(frqs, list)`. README.md:91 Quick Start builds `freqs = np.linspace(0.1, 2.0, 5000).astype(np.float32)`. (Behavior read from code; CE.run compiles a kernel first so it could not be executed on CPU.)
recommendation: Add one helper (e.g. utils._broadcast_freqs(freqs, n_lcs) accepting ndarray-of-any-float-dtype or list-of-arrays) and use it in LS/CE/PDM run/batched_run_const_nfreq/large_run; unit-test it on CPU. Re-run the CE GPU tests.

title: keplerian_freq_grid/uniform_freq_grid return float32 grids while every other grid builder returns float64, and float32 trial frequencies degrade reported phi0 by up to ~0.07 cycles on BJD-scale data (per the project's own CHANGELOG analysis); README Quick Start teaches the float32 cast
evidence: bls_frequencies.py:108 `freqs = np.array(freqs, dtype=np.float32)` and :161 `.astype(np.float32)` (documented :87 `freqs : ndarray, float32`); probe: `keplerian_freq_grid ... dtype=float32` vs `transit_autofreq ... dtype0=float64`, `utils.autofrequency ... dtype=float64`, `period_grid_ofir ... dtype=float64`. Phases are re-referenced with the CALLER's frequencies: bls.py:1621 `qphi_sols = [(q, (phi + (epoch * freq)) % 1.0) for (q, phi), freq in zip(qphi_sols, freqs)]`; CHANGELOG.rst:43: `sparse_bls_cpu/sparse_bls_gpu re-reference solution phases with the caller's float64 frequencies (the float32 copies put phases off by epoch*|f64-f32|, up to ~0.07 cycles at BJD epochs)`. README.md:85 `t = ... .astype(np.float32)` and :91 `freqs = ... .astype(np.float32)` — the Quick Start models float32 inputs as the norm, which combined with BJD times reintroduces the phase error the release notes say was fixed. All GPU paths cast internally anyway (bls.py:1524 `np.array(freqs).astype(np.float32)`, 2
recommendation: Return float64 from keplerian_freq_grid/uniform_freq_grid (and qvals), update their docstrings; drop the `.astype(np.float32)` casts from README.md:85,91 and test_readme_examples.py; add a one-line 'inputs may be float64; cast happens internally after float64 epoch subtraction' note to the BLS docs.

title: PDM legacy 4-tuple input treats the 3rd element as WEIGHTS (not dy) with only a DeprecationWarning and no removal version; a (t, y, dy, freqs) call silently returns a wrong periodogram
evidence: pdm.py:332-340: `is_deprecated = len(data) > 0 and len(data[0]) == 4` -> `warnings.warn("The (t, y, w, freqs) format is deprecated and will be removed in the future. ...", DeprecationWarning, stacklevel=2)`; pdm.py:346-348 legacy branch uses the tuple as-is; pdm.py:130 `t, y, w, freqs = data_cpu` (weights consumed directly, no `weights(err)` conversion, which only happens on the new path pdm.py:361-363). Every other process documents the 3rd element as `dy` (ce.py run docstring, lombscargle.py:783-786). No 'removed in <version>' anywhere: `grep -rn "removed in\|will be removed" cuvarbase/*.py CHANGELOG.rst docs/RELEASE_NOTES_v1.0.0.md` -> only pdm.py:335 'in the future'. Python hides DeprecationWarning by default unless triggered from __main__.
recommendation: Keep the shim through 1.x (the 4-tuple was the 0.2.x API) but: change to FutureWarning (visible by default), say 'removed in 2.0', and spell out in the message and pdm.rst:735-739 that the third element is interpreted as normalized weights, not uncertainties.

title: BLSMemory.allocate_pinned_arrays was renamed (with deprecation) but TLSMemory.allocate_pinned_arrays and the *_pinned_cpu methods on the other Memory classes were not — the rename added inconsistency instead of removing it
evidence: bls.py:506-510 `def allocate_pinned_arrays(...): """Deprecated alias for allocate_host_arrays.""" warnings.warn("allocate_pinned_arrays is deprecated; use allocate_host_arrays", DeprecationWarning)`; tls.py:255 `def allocate_pinned_arrays(self):` (canonical name on TLSMemory, no alias); ce_memory.py:122, lombscargle_memory.py:199, nfft_memory.py:126 `def allocate_pinned_cpu(self, **kwargs)`. title: tls_stats.signal_detection_efficiency keeps a silent `window_length` alias with no callers and no warning — remove before freezing

title: cuvarbase/core.py is labeled a backward-compat shim but is the primary import path for 5 of 8 GPU modules and is documented as a real module in the Sphinx API page

title: Two independent implementations of weights(): cuvarbase.utils.weights and cuvarbase.memory.lombscargle_memory.weights (different objects; LS imports one, PDM the other)

Note: This function is also available in cuvarbase.utils for backward compatibility.`; memory/__init__.py:17,26 re-exports the memory one. title: Conventions that differ across algorithms are documented nowhere in one place (return shapes, min-vs-max statistic, oversampling/nfreq/precision/batch_size names) and the RELEASE_NOTES batch_size row overstates its scope
evidence: Return types (AST dump/docstrings): eebls_gpu -> `(power, sols)`; eebls_gpu_fast/_optimized/_adaptive -> power only; eebls_transit/eebls_transit_gpu -> `(freqs, power, sols|None)`; eebls_gpu_batch -> `list of ndarray`; sparse_bls_* -> `(powers, sols)`; tls_search_* -> dict, tls_search_batch -> list of dict; LS/CE/PDM run -> `list of (freqs, power)`; NUFFT-LRT run -> 2-D/3-D SNR array. Sign: pdm.rst:646-652 `cuvarbase returns ... P(f) = 1 - Theta(f), so the best candidate frequencies appear as maxima ... consistent with the other periodograms in this package`, but CE is a minimum statistic (docs/source/plots/ce_example.py: `# Find the best frequency (that *minimizes* the conditional entropy)`). Oversampling is spelled four ways: `samples_per_peak` (bls.transit_autofreq, utils.autofrequency), `oversampling` (bls_frequencies.*, tls_grids.t0_grid), `oversampling_factor` (tls_grids.period_grid_ofir, tls_search_*), `oversample`/`t0_oversample`/`refine_oversample` (tls_grids.t0_grid_size, tls
recommendation: Do not rename anything. Add a short 'Conventions' page to docs/source (linked from index.rst) with one table: inputs `(t, y, dy)`, freqs [cycles/day] vs periods [days] per algorithm, return shape per entry point, 'maximum is best' except CE, which names mean oversampling, precision availability, batch_size defaults. Amend the RELEASE_NOTES table: batch_size row -> 'LombScargleAsyncProcess only', pinned row -> 'LS/CE/NFFT/BLS-batch', and add the eebls_transit_gpu 3-tuple row.

title: No stated API-stability / deprecation policy for the 1.x line (what is public, what 'experimental' means, when aliases are removed)
evidence: `grep -nEi "deprecat|semver|stable|backward" CONTRIBUTING.md` -> no matches; `grep -nEi "deprecat|semver|api|freeze|__all__" analysis/RELEASE_RUNBOOK_v1.0.0.md` -> no matches; RELEASE_NOTES has a migration table but no statement of what 1.0 promises; the only removal timeline in the codebase is pdm.py:335 'will be removed in the future'. Experimental surfaces exist without a policy: nufft_lrt (import warning), bls.hone_solution (`Experimental!`), tls_stats.false_alarm_probability 'empirical' (docstring warning: 'NOT calibrated').
recommendation: Add a 6-line 'API stability' section to RELEASE_NOTES (and CONTRIBUTING): public = names in each module's __all__ and the top-level __all__; experimental (no stability promise) = cuvarbase.nufft_lrt, bls.hone_solution, the 'empirical' FAP heuristic; deprecated aliases (PDM 4-tuple, BLSMemory.allocate_pinned_arrays, cuvarbase.<bls name> fallback) stay through 1.x and go in 2.0.

title: Inverted/degenerate grid bounds are accepted silently and empty inputs raise untyped ZeroDivisionError or numpy-internal messages, contrary to the 'typed exceptions with clear messages' promise
evidence: Probe (CPU, conftest stubs): `keplerian_freq_grid pmin>pmax  OK ndarray shape=(0,)`; `uniform_freq_grid pmin>pmax  OK ndarray shape=(1,)`; `period_grid_ofir pmin>pmax  OK ndarray shape=(100,)` (a 100-point grid for an impossible range); `keplerian_freq_grid baseline=0  RAISE ZeroDivisionError`; `eebls_transit empty (cpu sparse)  RAISE ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero`; `transit_autofreq empty  RAISE ZeroDivisionError`; `t0_grid_size q=0  RAISE ZeroDivisionError`; `period_grid_ofir single t  RAISE ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer` (+4 numpy divide warnings); `sparse_bls_cpu empty data  RAISE ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation minimum which has no identity`; `tls_stats.false_alarm_probability bad method  OK` (tls_stats.py:245-258 `if method == 'gaussian': ... else:` treats any string as 'empirical'). RELEASE_NOTES 'Usability': `Typed exceptions (ValueError/RuntimeError) with clear messages replace bare Exceptions and asserts`.
recommendation: In keplerian_freq_grid/uniform_freq_grid/period_grid_ofir raise ValueError for period_min >= period_max, baseline <= 0, len(t) < 2; in false_alarm_probability raise ValueError for unknown method; route empty/short inputs through the shared lightcurve validator from the NaN finding. All CPU-testable; add to test_bls_frequencies.py / a new test_tls_grids.py.
